title:
PYTHAGORAS,
(FINDING A SHORTER SIDE)
objective: LO: I can use Pythagoras' theorem to find a shorter side of a right-angled triangle.

content.text: When the hypotenuse and one shorter side are known, rearrange Pythagoras to find the other: a² = c² − b².
Remember: Always subtract the known shorter side squared from the hypotenuse squared. The hypotenuse is the longest side.

key_idea.title: Key idea
key_idea.text: Rearrange a² + b² = c² to a² = c² − b², then take the square root.
key_idea.caption: Subtract known shorter side squared from hypotenuse squared

modelled_examples.label: Example 1 – integer answer
modelled_examples.question: Find side a if c = 10 and b = 8.
modelled_examples.explanation: Always square both known sides first, then subtract.

modelled_examples.label: Example 2 – non-integer answer
modelled_examples.question: Find side a if c = 9 and b = 5.
modelled_examples.explanation: If the answer is not a perfect square, round appropriately.

modelled_examples.label: Example 3 – in context
modelled_examples.question: A rope 17 m long is tied to the top of a 15 m pole and pulled taut to the ground. How far from the base is it?
modelled_examples.explanation: Identify the hypotenuse (always the longest side), then subtract.

modelled_examples.label: Example 4 – checking which is the hypotenuse
modelled_examples.question: A triangle has sides 20 cm, 16 cm, and an unknown third side. The 20 cm side is the hypotenuse. Find the third side.
modelled_examples.explanation: The hypotenuse is always stated or identified as the longest/opposite the right angle.

practice.heading: Finding a (decimal answers)
practice.instruction: Find the missing side to 1 d.p.

practice.instruction: Solve each problem. Round to 1 d.p. where needed.

questions.expression: Right triangle: hypotenuse 14, one leg 6. Other leg?
Right triangle: hypotenuse 11, one leg 7. Other leg?

items.statement: To find a shorter side, rearrange to a² = c² − b²
a = c − b gives the missing side
The hypotenuse is always the longest side in a right-angled triangle
a² = c² + b² when finding a shorter side
If the answer is not exact, round to an appropriate degree of accuracy

problems.text: A right-angled triangle has hypotenuse (2x + 1) cm and legs x cm and (x + 7) cm. Use Pythagoras to form an equation and find x. Hence find all three side lengths.
Two vertical poles are 8 m and 14 m tall, standing 8 m apart on level ground. A wire connects the tops of the two poles. Find the length of the wire.
